pr_title: Move UI tests from controller to system spec

issue_context.title: Review & Refactor OAuth Specs
issue_context.body:
All those new examples [here](https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/31129) seem to test the user interface and as such do not belong in a "controller spec".

There are two alternative options:

* If you just want to make sure certain things are present in the html template, then a "view spec" would be the correct place. Additionally you _could_ add a test here that makes sure the controller actually renders that template.
* If you want to make sure that a certain kind of client request leads to the UI being in a certain state, this should be a "system spec". If you go down that route, you might want to have these be "driven_by" `:rack_test` which is a lot faster than spinning up a browser for this (see https://rspec.info/features/6-0/rspec-rails/system-specs/system-specs/)

_Originally posted by @oneiros in https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/31129#discussion_r1691002607_

review_comments: Small style feedback -- pull this and the line below out into private methods instead of local vars (the same selector is used in this example and the one in the context below)?

I get and respect your point. I am however not convinced that this would help the readability of this spec. I like using the syntax possibilities rspec gives me (sometimes a bit too much :grimacing:), but mostly believe in "stupid" and explicit test code, even if that is not super "DRY".
